finding.summary: Cell-style clear semantics changed but the canonical tables design doc was not updated (still shows `backgroundColor=""` as a stored cell attribute)
finding.evidence: This delta adds `removedCellStyleAttrs` + `removeStyleByPath` to `applyCellStyle` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:249,2432), establishing the convention that a cleared cell attribute is REMOVED from the Yorkie cell node rather than merged over with an empty value. The canonical subsystem doc `docs/design/docs/docs-tables.md` — the doc that specifies the cell node attribute set (lines 156-166) and shows the tree shape — still depicts `cell(backgroundColor="" …)` at line 138 and describes `backgroundColor` simply as "CSS color string" with no mention that clearing removes the attribute. Two design docs WERE updated in this PR (docs-docx-import-export.md, slides-pptx-export.md), so the omission is specific to the table cell-style contract this delta actually changes.

verdict.reason: The finding's code evidence checks out (removedCellStyleAttrs at yorkie-doc-store.ts:255-261, used by applyCellStyle at 2437-2452), but its design-fit premise does not. (a) The semantics it says are undocumented are already documented: docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md:238-241 states the store convention that an explicitly-`undefined` style value REMOVES the attribute, and docs/design/docs/docs-intent-preserving-edits.md:240-242 documents that convention for cell nodes specifically (applyCellSpan sets via styleByPath and clears via removeStyleByPath). (b) The canonical tables doc already expresses the model this delta conforms to: docs-tables.md:94-99 declares `backgroundColor?: string` as an OPTIONAL cell-style key (unset = absent), so "cleared = attribute gone" is consistent with, not contradicted by, the doc. (c) The `cell(backgroundColor="" …)` ASCII line at docs-tables.md:138 was already inaccurate before this delta: serializeCellStyle only writes the attribute when truthy (yorkie-doc-store.ts:238), and that function predates the change (the tables doc references it at line 419). Hence the empty string was never the persisted form and this delta establishes no new stored-attribute contract — it applies an existing, already-documented convention to a second surface. No architecture/data-model change occurred, so the design-doc-discipline trigger does not fire; the residual staleness in one illustrative diagram is a doc nit, which never blocks under this rubric.
